name: Forest Fody
rangeDescription: Forest of eastern madagascar
description: Sparrow-like weaver in which red-hooded breeding males are distinctive, but females and non-breeding females are drab. Madagascar endemic that is found in and adjacent to rainforest, sometimes in flocks that may include other birds.

name: Blue-and-white Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Halmahera, ternate, morotai, bacan, obi, and adjacent moluccas
description: A small kingfisher with bright azure-blue upperparts and a gleaming white underside. Female shows a diagnostic blue chest band.

name: Salim Ali's Swift
rangeDescription: Eastern tibetan plateau, western sichuan; winter range unknown
description: A large scimitar-winged swift of valleys, cliffs, and gorges. Nests in buildings and rock crevices; often gives a chattering scream when entering and leaving the nest.

name: Socotra Starling
rangeDescription: Rocky hills of socotra island (off northeastern somalia)
description: Large, glossy black starling with a strong bill. The tail is moderately long, and squared off.

name: Veraguan Mango
rangeDescription: Western panama (chiriquí to southern coclé) and adjacent islands
description: Rather large hummingbird with a slightly decurved bill, extremely similar to Green-breasted Mango, and range overlap is not perfectly understood. Apparently Veraguan Mango mostly replaces Green-breasted from the Osa Peninsula to Panama City.

name: Maleo
rangeDescription: Sulawesi including buton (off southeast), and formerly lembeh (just east of northern sulawesi)
description: A massive black-and-white megapode with a rose-pink breast and a diagnostic prominent knob on the nape. Found in lowland and hill forest, in areas near beaches or areas with volcanic sands in which they lay their eggs.

name: Damara Tern
rangeDescription: Coastal namibia to cape province; winters to northern angola
description: A very small, short-tailed tern of coastal waters. It often flies slowly on rapidly-beating wings with its head angled downwards, before hovering and plunge-diving to catch small fish.

name: Blacksmith Thrush
rangeDescription: Breeds southernmost brazil (north to paraná), northeastern argentina, and southeastern paraguay; winters northward to south-central brazil (northward to mato grosso and goiás)
description: A distinctive gray thrush found in lowlands of southeast Brazil and Paraguay. Males are gray-brown above and pale grayish below with a conspicuous streaked white throat, yellow bill, and yellow feet.

name: Sikkim Treecreeper
rangeDescription: Himalayas of nepal to southern tibet and northwestern india
description: Dark treecreeper with a warm rusty tail, thin white brow and mustache, and a gray chest. Warm tones on the tail contrast sharply with the cooler brown on the back and wings.

name: Greater Thornbird
rangeDescription: Northern brazil to northern bolivia, paraguay, and northern argentina
description: Large and bulky thornbird with a long tail, conspicuous yellow eyes, and a whitish throat. Cinnamon above and buff below.

name: Cape Verde Swamp Warbler
rangeDescription: Santiago (cape verde islands); extirpated on são nicolau and brava
description: Medium-sized warbler with a long bill, short wings, and a long tail, endemic to the Cape Verde Islands. Rather grayish above with a gray-brown wash below.

name: Malaysian Blue-banded Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar, malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Small, rather dark kingfisher. Male is highly distinctive, with a broad blue-green band across a white chest.

name: Planalto Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Northeastern argentina (missiones) and far southern brazil (southwestern paraná to southern rio grande do sul)
description: Small, nondescript bird that is usually very difficult to spot. Mostly dark gray with a cinnamon vent with dark bars.

name: Chestnut-throated Monal-Partridge
rangeDescription: Alpine mountain slopes of northeastern tibet
description: Large modestly-colored terrestrial bird of open woodlands, scrublands, and meadows in alpine areas. Brown overall with a peaked head, chestnut throat, and bright red skin around the eye.

name: Dark-sided Thrush
rangeDescription: Nepal to northern india, southwestern china, myanmar, thailand, and northern indochina
description: A dark sooty thrush with an unusually long bill. Dark brown overall with a pale crescent behind the ear and weak white spotting on the underparts.

name: Sulphur-throated Finch
rangeDescription: Arid littoral of southwestern ecuador and northwestern peru
description: Drab and nomadic finch-like bird found in desert and arid scrub in northwestern Peru and southwestern Ecuador. While some birds show a distinct yellowish wash on their face and throat and a short mustache, many individuals lack these features, and easily could be confused with female Parrot-billed Seedeater.

name: Black-throated Malimbe
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern ghana and southern cameroon to gabon and eastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A unique forest malimbe often seen high above the ground, particularly fond of swamp forest, palm trees, and other areas near water. Female is wholly black all over, while the male has bright red extending from the chest around to the back of the neck and up to the crown, surrounding a black throat and face.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Red-necked Avocet
rangeDescription: Locally in australia
description: Distinctive shorebird with very long and dramatically up-curved bill, dark red head and neck. In flight shows patches of black on the back, shoulders, and wing-tips.

name: White-faced Nunbird
rangeDescription: Locally in andean foothills of western colombia to northwestern peru
description: Rare and elusive denizen of Andean cloud forest; found at higher elevations than any other puffbird. Distinctive; note especially the stout, black bill bordered by white feathers, chestnut underparts, and red eye.

name: Black-fronted Ground-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of chile and argentina; winters northward to southern peru (arequipa)
description: Breeds locally in the high Andes of central Chile and adjacent Argentina; migrates north in winter. Favors bleak rocky and stony slopes, adjacent bogs, and lakeshores; often in same areas as other ground-tyrant species.
